ctx.x: And they had Leon Abbey. They had someone else whose name I can't remember at the moment. I can see his face before me, but I can't remember the name. MR. BERGER: Was the music you played there in this early time, early in the sense that it was in the early thirties, was that the kind of music that would be called Swing?

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Before that there had been a band there called Leon Abbey [phonetic].

ctx.x: Or was that later when you came back?

Maybe it was, yeah. Well, we had to play opposite somebody in 1928, even. Maybe it was Fess Williams. Before that there had been a band there called Leon Abbey [phonetic]. I don’t think we played opposite them. I think they played before we were there. But definitely Fess Williams, yes.
What was the book like of the . . . which was now billed, I think, as Benny Carter and His Playboys?
